claims.text: Standard TOR-TILD EAM references have insufficient phase-space overlap with ab initio configurations in high-temperature multicomponent alloys.
Insufficient phase-space overlap from standard EAM references causes larger thermodynamic-integration path mismatches.
A hybrid reference potential can smoothly blend a liquid-specialized potential with a solid-specialized potential.
The blending weights can be determined from local structural descriptors through a switching function.
Coordination numbers and bond-angle distributions can discriminate liquid-like from solid-like local environments.
A liquid-optimized potential will capture the diverse, transient local configurations sampled by the ab initio liquid.
A solid-optimized potential will maintain fidelity in ordered local regions.
Smooth local switching between liquid- and solid-specialized potentials will improve reference–ab initio phase-space overlap.
Improved phase-space overlap will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch.
The hybrid reference will reduce thermodynamic-integration mismatch by approximately 50% relative to standard TOR-TILD EAM references.
Free-energy differences obtained with the hybrid reference will converge to within approximately 15 meV/atom of full ab initio results.
The predicted latent heat will agree with the ab initio benchmark within approximately 15 meV/atom.
The proposed method applies to refractory and multicomponent high-entropy alloys from 0.95Tm to 1.05Tm.
MoNbTaW and similar systems exhibit transient liquid-like and persistent solid-like local order near melting.
Extensive ab initio benchmark data exist for both liquid and solid phases of the relevant refractory HEAs and related binary systems.
The method's validity outside the stated compositional space or substantially away from the melting point is uncertain.
